project.title: Pedestrian Truss Bridge — Conceptual Design Study
project.description: Fictional educational sample bundled with FrameLytix: a conceptual Pratt through-truss footbridge, 24.0 m clear span, used to demonstrate requirements, decision matrices, calculations and traceability.
project.author: FrameLytix Sample Team
project.scope: This is an educational conceptual study of a fictional 24.0 m pedestrian through-truss bridge. It demonstrates how FrameLytix records requirements, compares alternatives, documents calculations and traces evidence. All loads, limits and stresses are illustrative assumptions. It is not a professional design, has not been checked against any code and is NOT construction-ready.
project.summary: A fictional Pratt truss footbridge (6 panels x 4.0 m, 3.0 m deep, 2.5 m clear width) is used as a worked example. Under an illustrative 4.0 kPa load the line load is 10.0 kN/m, the midspan moment 720 kN·m, each reaction 120 kN and the conceptual chord force 240 kN. Warren scores highest in the truss decision matrix but fails a mandatory constraint, so Pratt is provisionally recommended. Several items remain open on purpose. This sample is not a professional design, is not checked against any code and is NOT FOR CONSTRUCTION.

requirements.title: Minimum clear span of 24.0 m
requirements.description: The bridge shall provide a clear span of at least 24.0 m between abutment faces to cross the creek channel.
requirements.acceptanceCriterion: Clear span measured between abutment faces is not less than 24.0 m.
requirements.verificationNotes: Span of 24.0 m measured from the illustrative site sketch (IMG-001) and confirmed against the general arrangement drawing DRW-001 REV-B.

requirements.title: Pedestrian live-load capacity
requirements.description: Design for an illustrative uniformly distributed pedestrian live load of 4.0 kPa. This value is an ASSUMPTION for the educational study and is not taken from any code.
requirements.acceptanceCriterion: Members sized so that the conceptual chord force check passes under 4.0 kPa (illustrative). Governing code loads to be confirmed.
requirements.notes: Load assumption not yet confirmed against the governing code; see RSK-001.

requirements.title: Clear deck width of at least 2.5 m
requirements.description: The walking surface shall provide at least 2.5 m clear width between truss inner faces.
requirements.acceptanceCriterion: Clear deck width is not less than 2.5 m.
requirements.verificationNotes: Clear width of 2.5 m between curbs confirmed on the cross-section of DRW-001 REV-B (trusses at 2.9 m centres).

requirements.title: Maximum floor-beam spacing of 4.0 m
requirements.description: Floor-beam spacing shall not exceed 4.0 m to suit the selected deck panel span.
requirements.acceptanceCriterion: Floor beams at every panel point with spacing not greater than 4.0 m.
requirements.verificationNotes: Inspection of DRW-001 REV-B shows 6 panels at 4.0 m with a floor beam at each panel point (VER-003).

requirements.title: Corrosion protection for de-icing-salt exposure
requirements.description: The structure shall have corrosion protection suitable for an environment exposed to de-icing salts.
requirements.acceptanceCriterion: Selected material and protection system judged suitable for de-icing-salt exposure by the team; to be confirmed by a qualified engineer.
requirements.notes: Material selection (ARG-002) done; protection strategy (ARG-005) needs revision.

requirements.title: Serviceability deflection limit (to be confirmed)
requirements.description: Mid-span deflection under pedestrian load shall be limited. The limit is to be confirmed against the governing code; no value is assumed here.
requirements.acceptanceCriterion: Limit to be confirmed against the governing code.
requirements.notes: UNVERIFIED mandatory constraint. Deflection and vibration have not been checked.

requirements.title: Minimize life-cycle maintenance
requirements.description: Prefer solutions that reduce inspection and repainting effort over the service life.
requirements.acceptanceCriterion: Maintenance burden compared qualitatively between alternatives.

requirements.title: Prefer road-transportable prefabricated modules
requirements.description: Prefabricated truss modules that can be moved by road are preferred to reduce on-site work.
requirements.acceptanceCriterion: Modules fit within typical road transport envelopes (to be confirmed).

requirements.title: Accessible approach slopes
requirements.description: Approach paths at both abutments should provide gentle slopes suitable for wheelchair and stroller use.
requirements.acceptanceCriterion: Approach slopes to be set against the governing accessibility guidance (to be confirmed).

requirements.title: Aesthetic integration with park setting
requirements.description: The structure should sit comfortably in the surrounding park landscape.
requirements.acceptanceCriterion: Qualitative review of finish and colour with the park owner.

arguments.title: Truss Configuration Selection
arguments.problemStatement: Select a truss configuration for a 24.0 m pedestrian through-truss that works with 4.0 m deck panels.
arguments.objective: Choose the configuration that best balances cost, strength and feasibility while meeting all mandatory constraints.

alternatives.name: Pratt truss
alternatives.description: Verticals in compression, diagonals in tension sloping toward midspan; 6 panels at 4.0 m.

alternatives.name: Warren truss
alternatives.description: No verticals, alternating diagonals; 4 panels at 6.0 m.

alternatives.name: Howe truss
alternatives.description: Diagonals in compression sloping away from midspan; verticals in tension; 6 panels at 4.0 m.

criteria.name: Cost
criteria.description: Initial cost; higher score = lower cost

scores.rationale: More members than a Warren truss, so somewhat higher fabrication cost.
Slender tension diagonals; short compression verticals; well-understood load path.
Panel points match the 4.0 m deck panel module; modular shop fabrication.
Fewest members and joints, so lowest cost.
Efficient load path, but longer unbraced members.
Simple to fabricate, but 6.0 m panels do not suit the deck module.
Similar member count to Pratt.
Long diagonals in compression need buckling attention.
Less common for steel; less familiar detailing.

constraintEvaluations.justification: Floor beams at 4.0 m panel points (see DRW-001).
Deflection limit not yet defined or checked.
6.0 m panels exceed the 4.0 m floor-beam spacing needed by the deck.
Deflection limit not yet defined or checked.
Floor beams at 4.0 m panel points.
Deflection limit not yet defined or checked.

assumptions: Truss depth is fixed at 3.0 m for all alternatives.
Deck sits at the bottom chord (through truss) with floor beams at panel points.
Scores are team judgements on a 1 to 5 scale; higher is always more favourable (including cost).
arguments.evidenceSummary: See CALC-004 for the chord force, DIA-001 for the configurations and MOD-001 for the concept model. No structural analysis of the alternatives has been performed.
arguments.selectionRationale: Warren has the highest weighted score (4.3) but fails mandatory REQ-004 and is therefore ineligible. Pratt (3.7) is the highest-scoring eligible alternative, provisionally, because REQ-006 is still unverified.
arguments.justification: Warren scores highest numerically (4.3 versus 3.7 for Pratt and 3.0 for Howe), mainly on cost. However its 6.0 m panels exceed the 4.0 m floor-beam spacing required by the deck (REQ-004), which is a mandatory constraint, so it is ineligible regardless of score. Pratt and Howe both meet REQ-001 and REQ-004; Pratt scores higher. The selection is provisional: the serviceability deflection limit (REQ-006) has not been confirmed or verified for any alternative.
arguments.risksAndLimitations: Scores are subjective team judgements. No analysis of deflection, vibration or member buckling has been done. A change to the deck module could reopen this decision.
arguments.author: FrameLytix Sample Team

revisions.author: FrameLytix Sample Team
revisions.summary: Added mandatory constraint evaluations; Warren found to fail REQ-004; selection changed to Pratt

arguments.title: Structural Material Selection
arguments.problemStatement: Select the primary structural material for the truss in a de-icing-salt environment.
arguments.objective: Pick a material that balances cost, strength, durability and maintainability while meeting corrosion protection needs (REQ-005).

alternatives.name: Galvanized structural steel
alternatives.description: Hot-dip galvanized rolled and welded steel sections.

alternatives.name: Weathering steel
alternatives.description: Atmospheric corrosion-resistant steel that forms a protective patina.

alternatives.name: Glued-laminated timber
alternatives.description: Engineered timber members with protective detailing.

scores.rationale: Galvanizing adds cost over bare steel.
Well-known strength and ductility.
Zinc coating gives long protection in most exposures.
Low maintenance with periodic inspection.
No coating cost.
Comparable strength to other structural steels.
Good in many atmospheres, but see REQ-005 evaluation.
Little repainting if the patina is stable.
Moderate cost; specialist supply.
Lower strength-to-size ratio; connections more demanding.
Needs careful moisture protection detailing.
Regular inspection and re-treatment likely.

constraintEvaluations.justification: Hot-dip galvanizing is judged suitable for de-icing-salt exposure (illustrative team judgement, to be confirmed by a qualified engineer).
Weathering steel is generally not recommended where de-icing salts cause persistent wet or salt exposure (illustrative team judgement, to be confirmed by a qualified engineer).
Suitability for salt exposure not yet established.

assumptions: De-icing salts will be used on approach paths and may reach the structure.
Judgements on suitability are illustrative team opinions, not code-based findings.
arguments.evidenceSummary: No test data. Judgements are based on general course knowledge; manufacturer literature is still to be obtained.
arguments.selectionRationale: Weathering steel scores highest numerically (4.2) but fails REQ-005 and is ineligible. Galvanized steel is the highest-scoring eligible alternative.
arguments.justification: Galvanized structural steel satisfies the corrosion mandate in REQ-005 and scores 3.75. Weathering steel scores higher but is ruled out by the salt-exposure constraint. Glulam remains unverified for REQ-005.
arguments.risksAndLimitations: The REQ-005 evaluation is an illustrative judgement and must be confirmed by a qualified engineer. Galvanized finish details are not developed.

calculations.title: Line load (w = q b)
calculations.purpose: Convert the illustrative pedestrian pressure into a line load per metre of span.
calculations.method: Multiply the pressure by the loaded width; 1 kPa x 1 m = 1 kN/m.
calculations.assumptions: Uniform pressure over the full clear deck width. 4.0 kPa is an illustrative assumption, not from a code.
calculations.reference: Standard statics relation for a simply supported span — see any introductory structural analysis text
calculations.verificationNotes: Hand-checked by a second team member: 4.0 x 2.5 = 10.0.
calculations.author: FrameLytix Sample Team

calculations.title: Midspan moment (M_max = wL²/8)
calculations.purpose: Maximum bending moment of a simply supported span under a uniform load.
calculations.method: Closed-form statics for a simply supported beam; truss treated as an equivalent beam.
calculations.assumptions: Simply supported; uniform load over the whole span; self-weight not included at this stage.
calculations.reference: Standard statics relation for a simply supported span — see any introductory structural analysis text
calculations.verificationNotes: Hand check by second team member (VER-002): 10 x 24^2 / 8 = 720. Load input still unconfirmed.
calculations.author: FrameLytix Sample Team

calculations.title: Support reaction (R = wL/2)
calculations.purpose: Vertical reaction at each support under the uniform load.
calculations.method: Symmetry of a simply supported span under a uniform load.
calculations.assumptions: Same as CALC-002. Reactions are per bridge (both trusses combined).
calculations.reference: Standard statics relation for a simply supported span — see any introductory structural analysis text
calculations.verificationNotes: Cross-checked against the load diagram DIA-002.
calculations.author: FrameLytix Sample Team

calculations.title: Chord force (F = M/h)
calculations.purpose: Conceptual chord force from the moment couple across the truss depth.
calculations.method: Resolve the moment into a force couple acting at the top and bottom chord centroids.
calculations.assumptions: Whole-bridge moment resolved into one chord couple; split between the two trusses and secondary effects are not considered.
calculations.reference: Standard statics relation for a simply supported span — see any introductory structural analysis text
calculations.author: FrameLytix Sample Team

calculations.title: Required chord area (A_req = F/σ_allow)
calculations.purpose: Order-of-magnitude chord area needed at an illustrative allowable stress.

variables.description: Chord force from CALC-004 (240 kN = 240000 N)

calculations.method: Axial stress check: area = force / allowable stress, with force in newtons and stress in N/mm².
calculations.assumptions: Illustrative allowable stress of 150 MPa; no buckling, connection, fatigue or load-factor effects considered. NOT a design check.
calculations.reference: Standard statics relation for a simply supported span — see any introductory structural analysis text
calculations.author: FrameLytix Sample Team

evidence.title: Span measurement from site sketch
evidence.summary: The 24.0 m clear span was measured between the abutment faces on the illustrative site sketch (IMG-001) and agrees with DRW-001 REV-B. Supports REQ-001.

evidence.title: Hand check of midspan moment (CALC-002)
evidence.summary: A second team member reproduced 720 kN·m by hand. The arithmetic is correct, but the 4.0 kPa live-load input is an unconfirmed assumption, so this only partially supports REQ-002.

evidence.title: Inspection of DRW-001: floor-beam spacing
evidence.summary: Inspection of DRW-001 REV-B shows a floor beam at each of the 7 panel points with 4.0 m spacing, meeting the maximum spacing of REQ-004.

risks.title: Live-load assumption not confirmed against governing code
risks.description: The 4.0 kPa pedestrian load is an illustrative assumption. The governing code may require a different load or additional cases.
risks.mitigation: Identify the governing code and confirm loads with a qualified engineer before any further design.

risks.title: Corrosion from de-icing salts
risks.description: Salt spray and run-off may accelerate corrosion of steel members and connections.
risks.mitigation: Galvanized steel (ARG-002) with a durability strategy (ARG-005, under revision).

risks.title: Deflection and vibration serviceability not yet checked
risks.description: Light pedestrian trusses can be lively; no limit has been set and no check performed.
risks.mitigation: Confirm limits (REQ-006), then run a deflection and natural-frequency check.

risks.title: Transport of prefabricated truss segments
risks.description: Modules may exceed road transport limits for width, height or mass.
risks.mitigation: Split the truss into modules sized for road transport; confirm with a fabricator.

risks.title: Scour at abutments
risks.description: Creek flows could erode abutment foundations.
risks.mitigation: Obtain hydrology and geotechnical information; set foundation depth accordingly.
